Cautiously optimistic tone: the FOMC highlights strengthening activity and employment alongside accommodative financial conditions, consistent with maintaining the policy rate at the zero lower bound and continuing large-scale asset purchases. The commitment to average inflation targeting (as articulated by Chair Powell in 2020) to let inflation run moderately above 2% aims to better anchor expectations and mitigate the classic Barro-Gordon inflation-bias problem while addressing ZLB constraints. The stance aligns with New Keynesian guidance and Clarida–Galí–Gertler/Taylor-principle frameworks that advocate looking through temporary, supply-driven inflation spikes and using forward guidance and QE to compress term premia. Implementation via the administered interest on reserve balances (IORB) is in line with Goodfriend’s (2002) emphasis on floor-system control of short rates. Still, the statement repeatedly flags virus-related downside risks. Netting these elements, the language is positive on growth but tempered by uncertainty, yielding a mildly positive overall sentiment.
